title: Spanish F-18 on NATO Air Policing Mission Shoots Down Suspected Russian Drone Over Romania Near Moldova Border
detail: Romanian surveillance systems detected an unidentified drone entering national airspace from Moldova at 04:44 local time on August 16, 2026, roughly 24km north of Galați. A Spanish Air and Space Force F/A-18 Hornet already airborne on a NATO air-policing patrol from the 57th Air Base at Mihail Kogălniceanu established radar contact and, after receiving authorization, shot the drone down at 05:01 over an uninhabited area between the villages of Băleni and Cudalbi in Galați County; all-clear was issued at 05:20. NATO's military headquarters said the drone appears to be Russian — the fourth such shootdown over Romania this year. Romanian Defense Minister Radu Miruță called the intercept a "tangible security guarantee based on vigilance, rapid response and solidarity among the countries of the Alliance," noting Romania's 614km border with Ukraine puts it "on the front line of the European Union's defence." The episode is notable for this tracker's Article 5 reliability theme: it was a non-US ally's jet, not a US asset, that defended NATO airspace, reinforcing the alliance's pivot toward European-led collective response as the Pentagon's Europe force-posture review continues.
